papers.title: Bidirectional Empowerment of Metamorphic Testing and Large Language Models: A Systematic Survey
papers.authors: Zheng Zheng, Zenghui Zhou, Yinwang Xu, Daixu Ren, Tsong Yueh Chen
papers.core_contribution: Taxonomizes metamorphic testing for LLMs and the use of LLMs to construct metamorphic tests across 93 primary studies.
papers.methodology: Systematic review of 93 primary studies, divided into metamorphic testing for LLM-based systems and LLM assistance for metamorphic-test construction.
papers.key_results: Metamorphic testing is established for oracle-deficient LLM applications, including autonomous agents, but the abstract and taxonomy do not identify security invariance under validated orchestration-graph rewrites as an evaluated setting.
papers.limitations: A May-2026 arXiv survey rather than a peer-reviewed graph-security experiment; breadth does not establish that every primary study lacks an adjacent formulation.
papers.math_foundations: Metamorphic relations specify necessary relations among outputs of related executions when a direct test oracle is unavailable.
papers.motivation: LLM outputs are open-ended and probabilistic, making exact per-input oracles difficult.
papers.constraints_inferred: The taxonomy combines heterogeneous tasks and relation-quality standards; construct validity remains relation-specific.
papers.key_decisions: Separates testing LLM systems with metamorphic relations from using LLMs to discover and implement those relations.
papers.tried_and_discarded: Not reported in the abstract-level extraction.
papers.load_bearing_assumptions: The 93-study search is sufficiently broad to characterize the field and the stated taxonomy distinguishes the relevant directions.
papers.relevance_reason: Closest 2026 synthesis for the method family; establishes crowding while leaving the proposed orchestration-security relation sharper.

papers.title: LLMORPH: Automated Metamorphic Testing of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Steven Cho, Stefano Ruberto, Valerio Terragni
papers.core_contribution: Automates input-level metamorphic testing for LLM NLP tasks using configurable transformations and output relations.
papers.methodology: Implements 36 metamorphic relations over four NLP tasks and evaluates GPT-4, Llama3, and Hermes 2 in 561,267 executions; manually inspects 937 violations.
papers.key_results: The evaluation reports an 18% average failure rate, while relation/task-specific false-positive rates in the manual sample range from 0% to 70%, demonstrating that relation validity is load-bearing.
papers.key_results_location: arXiv HTML lines 151-153; implementation and relation-validity discussion lines 59-64
papers.limitations: Input/output NLP relations often rely on semantic thresholds or LLM-generated transformations; the paper does not manipulate orchestration graphs or measure security contracts.
papers.math_foundations: A relation maps a source input to follow-up inputs and specifies the output relation that should hold; a violation is a fault candidate, not automatically a true defect.
papers.motivation: Metamorphic relations address the missing-oracle problem without labeled ground truth.
papers.constraints_inferred: False positives depend strongly on relation and task, so approximate semantic equivalence cannot support a security-regression claim without independent validation.
papers.key_decisions: Uses relation-specific verification restrictions and reports every source/follow-up output plus relation verdict in JSON.
papers.tried_and_discarded: Implements 36 of a 191-relation catalog based on applicability and implementation considerations.
papers.load_bearing_assumptions: The chosen output comparator and any LLM-based transformation reliably instantiate the intended relation.
papers.relevance_reason: Provides direct empirical evidence for both the power and relation-validity risk of LLM metamorphic testing; motivates OMST's exact pre-security eligibility gate.
